topic: understanding the concept of compound interest

easy.text: What distinguishes compound interest from simple interest?

options.text: Compound interest is calculated on both the original principal AND any previously earned interest
options.feedback: Correct -- this 'interest on interest' effect is what makes compound interest grow faster than simple interest over time.

options.text: Compound interest is only calculated on the original principal amount
options.feedback: That describes SIMPLE interest, not compound interest, which includes previously earned interest in later calculations.

options.text: Compound interest is always a fixed dollar amount every year
options.feedback: Compound interest amounts actually grow each period since it's a percentage applied to a growing balance, not a fixed dollar amount.

options.text: Compound interest and simple interest are just two names for the identical calculation
options.feedback: These are two genuinely different calculation methods -- compound interest includes interest-on-interest, while simple interest does not.

medium.text: You invest $1,000 at 10% annual compound interest. How much will you have after 2 years? (Formula: A = P(1+r)^t)

options.feedback: This is what SIMPLE interest would give (1000 + 100 + 100), not compound interest, which also earns interest on the first year's interest.
This is the balance after only ONE year, not after two years of compounding.
This is just the original principal, without any interest applied at all.

hard.text: Two people each invest $1,000 for 3 years. Person A earns 10% simple interest annually; Person B earns 10% compound interest annually. Approximately how much MORE does Person B end up with compared to Person A?

options.feedback: This doesn't correctly result from calculating and comparing both the simple and compound interest totals over 3 years.

options.text: Exactly $0 more -- they would end up with the same amount
options.feedback: Simple and compound interest produce genuinely different totals over multiple years (except in year 1) -- they wouldn't be equal after 3 years.
This significantly overestimates the actual difference between the two calculated totals.

easy.hard: This calculation method incorporates previously accumulated interest into the base for subsequent interest calculations.
easy.medium: This method calculates interest on your growing balance, not just your starting amount.

hard.medium: Calculate the simple interest total (1000 + 100 three times) and the compound interest total (1000×1.10×1.10×1.10), then subtract.
